newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In a rare show of unity, opposition politicians, Church representatives, leftist groups and businessmen yesterday assailed plans by certain quarters to amend the Constitution to give President Fidel Ramos a second term in office. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)

- Former President Corazon Aquino cautioned President Fidel Ramos against yielding to pressures to amend the 1987 Constitution and extend the presidential term limit, saying such moves could pave the way for return to dictatorial rule. (MANILA TIMES)

- An angry President Fidel Ramos on Monday lashed at his critics accusing them of dividing the people by sowing intrigues and spreading wild and unfounded rumours of a possible Malacanang-led coup. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)

- President Fidel Ramos denied on Monday that he was laying the groundwork for a military takeover to perpetuate himself in power and stressed that martial rule will never happen during his administration. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Engineering Equipment Inc posted a net income of 264.2 million pesos in 1996 from the year-ago 152.5 million pesos. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The Philippines' benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate rose to an average of 10.661 percent at the regular weekly auction from the previous 10.653 percent, the Bureau of Treasury said on Monday. (TODAY)
- Unaudited net income of Reynolds Philippines Corp in 1996 rose to 190.2 million peso from 107.43 million pesos in the previous year. (MANILA TIMES)
